newsitem.title: GERMANY: DIW - Productivity key in west German wage talks.
newsitem.headline: DIW - Productivity key in west German wage talks.

text.p: Wage settlements in west Germany concentrate more on productivity of firms than wage deals in other industrialised countries, helping German competiteveness, the DIW economic research institute said on Wednesday.
In a special report on wages, the DIW said German pay negotiations should continue to focus on productivity levels and not on exchange rate developments.

In recent years, west German unit wage costs, adjusted to take exchange rate fluctuations into account, have risen for the most part more slowly than elsewhere, the institute -- one of Germany's six leading research bodies -- said in the report.
It said that wage levels had therefore increased the competitiveness of German firms, not decreased it.
Since the introduction of free-floating exchange rates in 1973, wage costs in other countries had on average risen twice as much as in west Germany, the report said.

At the same time, productivity had grown more strongly in Germany than elsewhere, despite several periods of appreciation in the mark on foreign exchange markets which had harmed the competitiveness of west Germany, it added.
